newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VEERAKESARI
Sri Lanka does not get military assistance from foreign nations to fight separtist Tamil guerrillas, Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar tells BBC in London.
Major General Asoka Jayawardena, currently director-general, general staff, named new overall operations commander for north and east where the army is fighting the LTTE.
THINAKARAN
President Chandrika Kumaratunga allocates one billion rupees from the president's fund for nation-wide poverty alleviation programme.
DAILY NEWS
Sri Lanka air force wins national quality award for 1996, which puts in on par with American and British air forces, commander Oliver Ranasinghe says.
Sri Lanka to set up two dairy factories with the Indian National Dairy Development Board aiming to achieve self-sufficiency in milk.
THE ISLAND
National carrier Airlanka increases air fares to all destinations, except India, by 10 to 15 percent. Air fares to India were increased a few months ago.

Tamil rebels execute a 50 year-old man after tying him to a lamp post for allegedly being an imformant for security forces. Lamp post killings were common in 1980s in northern Jaffna peninsula when Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) executed hundreds of informants and rival group members.
LANKADEEPA
Forty six parliamentarians from the main opposition United National Party say they are willing to accept government invitation to go to Jaffna peninsula.
DINAMINA
Government preparing gazette notification announcing the banning of the LTTE, sources close to government say.
Government takes steps to give 400 scholarships to children of soldiers fighting Tamil guerrillas.
DIVAINA
Military plans to buy six specially equipped aircraft to monitor ships smuggling arms and ammunition for Tamil rebels, defence sources say.
--Colombo newsroom tel 941-434319
